seo_title: Why is my Mysore masala dosa not crispy? | SattvaSrsti

humanized.hook: Crispy dosas are a delight, but they can be tricky.
humanized.useful_answer: To achieve a crispy Mysore masala dosa, ensure your batter is flowy—not watery or thick. A well-heated iron tawa is crucial; sprinkle water to check if it sizzles before spreading the batter. Oil around the edges helps with crispness, but too much oil can make it greasy. Remember, a good Mysore dosa is crisp outside and slightly soft inside, not a paper-thin roast.
humanized.story: Imagine preparing a Mysore masala dosa, excited for that perfect crisp. But when you flip it, it’s soft and sad instead of golden and crunchy.
humanized.emotional_ending: With these tips, your next Mysore masala dosa can be a crispy triumph. Enjoy the deliciousness that comes with practice.

related_problems.q: What makes Mysore masala dosa different from regular masala dosa?
related_problems.a: The difference is the fiery red chilli-garlic chutney smeared inside before the potato filling.

related_problems.q: Why does my dosa stick to the pan?
related_problems.a: Pan neither too hot nor too cold — water should sizzle, not explode into steam.

related_problems.q: Should dosa batter be thick or thin?
related_problems.a: For crisp dosa, batter should pour like thin cream / thin pancake batter — spreadable, not stiff.

related_problems.q: Why does the potato filling make my dosa soggy?
related_problems.a: Add potato masala only at the end, once the dosa has set.
